answer: Each epoch a node must first allocate 32GB of dedicated RAM and commit one unique Blake3 state root over it, so two nodes claiming the same identity produce divergent hashes. A verifier then replays a random slice of that committed array against the stored root, checking the kernel-level memory map proves sole ownership; a duplicate root or a stale map fails instantly and the identity is evicted. Forging 5000 sybils means 160TB of genuine RAM held through full epochs, roughly $96000 monthly in ferrous-backed hardware, while honest single nodes pass on one marble of committed state.
